*   **Compact Surfaces:** The model tends to utilize more Gaussians to reconstruct compact surfaces because color depends on the normal attribute, making opacity L1 regularization critical to neutralize this effect [S1].

The claim states that the model uses more Gaussians for compact surfaces because color depends on the normal attribute, and that opacity L1 regularization is critical to neutralize this effect. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Because the color represented by editable Gaussians depends on the normal attribute, the model tends to utilize more Gaussians to reconstruct compact surfaces than base 3DGS. To neutralize this effect, we encourage the opacity of Gaussians to be as low as possible by adding an L1 regularization term.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
supported
*   **Performance:** Enables real-time scene editing (recoloring, opacity adjustment, light direction) without retraining [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the palette color parameter ($c_p$) 'can be adjusted during inference to achieve scene recoloring,' which supports the claim of real-time scene editing for recoloring. The model is parameterized with shading attributes (ambient, diffuse, specular coefficients, shininess) and geometry attributes (including opacity). While the text does not explicitly use the phrase 'light direction,' the inclusion of directional shading components (diffuse/specular coefficients) and the ability to adjust these parameters during inference implies the capability for lighting adjustments. The claim of 'without retraining' is supported by the distinction between the 'training' phase (where parameters are optimized) and 'inference' phase (where $c_p$ is adjusted), implying that editing occurs post-training. All specific facts mentioned in the claim are present in the evidence.
